summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, GERD, and tobacco use was admitted for evaluation of positional chest pressure and shortness of breath that worsened when lying down. Initial concerns included cardiac ischemia, but serial troponins were negative, EKG showed no acute changes, and a stress test revealed no ischemic ST changes, making acute coronary syndrome unlikely. A chest X-ray was normal, and D-dimer was negative, ruling out pulmonary embolism. Symptoms improved with albuterol nebulizers, suggesting bronchospasm, and mildly elevated inflammatory markers along with a recent upper respiratory infection raised suspicion for viral pericarditis. She was treated with colchicine and discharged with an albuterol inhaler for symptom management. Her home medications were resumed, and she was advised to follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing evaluation.
